supersedesOnly.reason: The backend may need to distinguish conversational correction from literal replacement, but that does not require separate participant controls when one free-form input can carry both intents explicitly.

observedFailure.mechanism: The repair correctly removed the explanatory-revision button but preserved a second 'exact wording' button because the storage contract was technically different. observedFailure.logicLesson: Do not multiply user controls merely because the backend has multiple intent classes. If one flexible input can express the distinction unambiguously, keep one interaction channel and infer or explicitly mark the narrower intent within it. Product semantics should determine controls, not implementation-state taxonomy.

repairDirection: Use the always-visible synthesis textbox as the single participant text-entry channel for disagreement, nuance, correction, missing context, or replacement wording.
